item.title: The Island That Held Them
item.description: In David Greig’s novel The Book of I, a monk, a Viking, and a ‘mead wife’ navigate a world torn between paganism and Christianity.

item.title: Artistic License
item.description: When an angel in a recently restored Roman chapel was seen to resemble Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, it touched off a very Italian scandal.

item.title: Diversity by Other Means
item.description: Progressives may have lost the battle for racial affirmative action, but ironically, Supreme Court decisions should allow colleges to give advantage to groups defined by their income, geography, or heritage.

item.title: Who Speaks for Us?
item.description: The representatives of our two-party system have made it into a weapon that works against the people.

item.title: The Docteur Is In
item.description: In January 1960 Brussels hosted a “Round Table” conference of Congolese and European leaders to negotiate the future of the Belgian Congo.
